steward_case_relevance_audit.purpose: Map Chapter 9 against every financial event in the steward's 16-year record, starting with the Honeysuckle $605K sale ($465K equity → $109K), the dissolution judgment with Christina, and every settlement that may have rested on incomplete PDD or FDD. For each: (1) Was a conforming PDD served with particularity and two years of tax returns? (2) Was a conforming FDD served with § 2105(b)(1)-(4) content? (3) If waived, did the § 2105(d) waiver meet all five representations? (4) Is there evidence of post-separation investment/business nondisclosure routing to § 2556? (5) Was § 2102(c) I&E compliance maintained for support calculation purposes?

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Retrieve PDDs from every dissolution and legal-separation file in the record. Verify: Judicial Council form in force at time of service, two years of tax returns attached, § 2104(c) particularity met, I&E accompanying, § 2104(f) timing met, proof of service filed.
For every judgment in the record, verify FDD served or § 2105(d) waiver executed with all five representations. Test waiver for (d)(5) set-aside acknowledgment — the most-frequently-missing element.

Identify any investment, business, or income-producing opportunity that surfaced to either spouse post-separation and was traceable to pre-separation activity. Nondisclosure routes gain to § 2556; if present, § 2556 omitted-asset motion is available.
factor_audits.audit_status: FLAGGED — cross-reference to FAMLAW property-financial-fraud findings.

factor_audits.audit_recommendation: Review all support orders and modifications for contemporaneous I&E on file. Missing, stale, or internally inconsistent I&E supports § 271 sanctions and support-order challenges.

Where nondisclosure evidence is strong and intent is provable, a separate § 1101 civil action (100% asset remedy for willful breach) may be viable in addition to Chapter 9 set-aside. Honeysuckle sale fraud is a leading candidate.
